slides.text:
In Go the type comes after the name, for the parameters and for the result. Names that share a type share one declaration. No result type means the function returns nothing.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.

Go reads the whole file, so a function can be written below the code that calls it.

A call never converts an argument for you, and a function with a result must return on every path.

exercises.title: Declare a function
exercises.guide: Write a function that adds two numbers and call it.

chunks.guide: The type comes after the name. `a, b int` gives both names one type, and the result type goes before the brace.

notes.text: The result type goes after the parameters.

exercises.title: Mixed types, no result
exercises.guide: Write a function with two kinds of parameter and nothing to return.

chunks.guide: Names of different types cannot share a type: each group gets its own. With no result type, nothing is returned.

notes.text: Each group of names gets its own type.
No result type, so nothing is returned.

chunks.guide: A function that returns nothing is called as a statement.

exercises.title: Complete the signature
exercises.guide: Give the parameter and the result their types.

exercises.title: No automatic conversion
exercises.guide: Pass an int to a function that wants a float.

chunks.guide: The parameter and the result are both `float64`.
`half` takes a `float64`. An `int` is never converted for you, so convert it in the call.

notes.text: Without it, the call does not compile.

exercises.title: Every path returns
exercises.guide: Write a function whose result depends on a chain of conditions.

chunks.guide: Two branches return a value, but a number can match neither.
Go checks that every path ends in a `return`. This one covers the numbers no branch matched.

notes.text: Without it, Go reports a missing return.

exercises.title: What does it print?
options: It does not compile: `count` is unused
exercises.explanation: An unused parameter is allowed. Only unused local variables and unused imports are errors, so the program compiles and prints `item: tea`.
